title: Evaluate continuous-output stability and external-integration compatibility for newly onboarded models
creator: Aisha Khan
description: Goal: Verify that newly onboarded model artifacts (vX.y variants) behave correctly under continuous streaming output and when invoked with external function/tool call flows, and produce publishable performance profiles for the model catalog. This ticket covers: (1) compatibility checks for function/tool-call semantics over streaming outputs, (2) token-stream alignment and truncation behavior with KV-prefetching and batching enabled, and (3) publishing a concise performance matrix and recommended version-pinning guidance for users.
acceptance_criteria: Create an automated compatibility matrix that runs against the onboarding snapshot (vX.y) and reports pass/fail for streaming+function-call combinations
Define token-level fidelity checks: chunk boundary integrity, no duplicated or missing function-call tokens, and preserved argument structure in streamed function calls
Publish performance profile (P50/P95 latency, tokens/sec, memory footprint) for both streaming and non-streaming routes in the catalog format
Integrate canary harness to run 1,000 synthetic streaming sessions and 200 replayed customer sessions; failure rate < 0.5% for critical invariants
Document recommended version-pinning strategy for customers when we publish model-variants and fallbacks
test_plan: Extend the existing streaming regression harness (repo: github.com/redwood-inference/stream-harness) with function-call replay support
Add KV-prefetch toggles (on/off/partial) to test matrix and measure token alignment across 3 sequence-length distributions
Run synthetic tests (edge cases: nested function calls, interleaved tool outputs, premature stream termination) and capture token diffs
Execute replay tests using sanitized traces from ops (dashboard) to validate real traffic patterns
Collect metrics to the canary dashboard: token_latency_ms (P50/P95), stream_dropout_rate, function_call_integrity_failures, model_memory_mb
technical_notes: Potential tradeoff: enabling aggressive KV prefetch reduces token latency but can alter streaming chunk boundaries; define a compatibility mode to preserve chunking semantics at cost of some latency
Backpressure handling: ensure runtime does not drop or reorder buffered function-call messages when client disconnects and reconnects; add idempotency markers in test vectors
Quantized variants: some 8-bit quantized builds change attention kernel timing; include those builds in the perf profile to avoid publishing misleading latencies
Fallback policy: if streaming function-call path fails, system should automatically fall back to non-streaming function-call execution for that request and emit an alert
implementation_steps: 1) Prototype compatibility checks in stream-harness: add a FunctionCallValidator module
2) Create a 5x5 test matrix (kv_prefetch x batching x client_buffering x sequence_length x quant_mode)
3) Wire harness results into canary-dashboard and create pass/fail thresholds
4) Run nightly canary runs for 7 days and gather aggregated metrics
5) Draft the model catalog entry and recommended version-pinning guidance, submit for PM review
